thread:
marta: quick summary — after last week's kernel bump (5.19.12) we saw a small but persistent uptick in Xid events on ~12 hosts in the us-west1 GPU pool. putting notes here so oncall + infra can iterate.
marta: symptoms: mid-run Xid 13/45 style crashes, sometimes paired with ECC correctable counts rising. not all cards on a host fail, seems card-specific.
alex: can you paste the host list and driver/kernel combo?
marta: hosts: gw-usw1-gpu-045, -067, -089, -112, -118, -121, -130, -142, -151, -160, -172, -179. driver: nvidia-driver 535.86, kernel 5.19.12-rc1. firmware versions vary (nv-fw 52.34/52.41).
ben: thanks. did we run the nightly GPU burnin on those after the kernel roll?
marta: yes — 8h burnin passed for 9/12, but the three worst hosts had intermittent hangs during synthetic-latency workloads (tail latency increase then Xid).
loren: I kicked off a quick bisect this morning across kernel versions and drivers. early data:
loren: - kernel 5.19.8 + driver 535.86 -> baseline: low Xid rate (~0.3/day)
loren: - kernel 5.19.12 + driver 535.86 -> spike (~6/day on affected hosts)
loren: - kernel 5.19.12 + driver 540.14 (pre-release) -> reduced (~1/day)
loren: so preliminary signal points to a kernel+driver interaction, not purely hw.
ben: good find. do we have dmesg snippets or nvml logs from the crash windows?
marta: pasted excerpts: ```
[  125.432123] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=2034, GPU=0, GPU-board: 0x319d
[  125.432456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  125.432789] kernel: watchdog: GPU hung, dump: ...
```
ben: Xid 31 often correlates with driver hang/timeout. Are ECC correctable counters jumping before these?
marta: yes — sample from gw-usw1-gpu-089: ECC correctable increased by ~210 in the 10m before the Xid.
alex: timeline/rollout plan? we should avoid mass revert; impact on capacity matters (we're at 78% gpu utilization in us-west1).
ben: propose this plan:
ben: 1) stabilize canary: boot a small canary subgroup with kernel 5.19.8 + driver 535.86 (revert kernel) to confirm drop.
ben: 2) test forward driver: boot the affected hosts with kernel 5.19.12 + driver 540.14 to validate reduced Xid.
ben: 3) if 2) passes for 48h, schedule rollout with gradated policy (10%->50%->full) and monitor Xid/ECC metrics.
ben: 4) failing cards where Xid persists -> schedule drain + replace.
alex: agree. any region constraints? if we drain 12 hosts we'll lose ~11% of capacity in the canary pool. can we shift workloads to eu-central1 temporarily? cross-region shift would increase network egress costs and latency for some customers.
marta: we can shift low-priority batch jobs. production latency-sensitive traffic should stay on healthy hosts.
loren: on the bisect side I also ran a kernel boot param tweak: `nvidia.NVreg_ResmanSigKill=0` and `nvidia.NVreg_EnablePCIeGen3=1` — small effect but not sufficient alone.
loren: I also saw that firmware nv-fw 52.41 + driver 540.14 + kernel 5.19.12 had the cleanest runs in our short 24h synthetic.
ci-bot: [test-run] gpu-burnin/us-west1/gw-usw1-gpu-067: pass (24h), Xid_count=0, ECC_corr_delta=12
ci-bot: [test-run] gpu-burnin/us-west1/gw-usw1-gpu-089: fail (10h), Xid_count=4, ECC_corr_delta=210
ben: note: gw-usw1-gpu-089 seems borderline — firmware update candidate then rerun. if fw update not possible (BSOD risk for non-upgradable hw) we plan drain/replace.
marta: I'm going to tag the affected hosts in inventory and open a ticket for firmware upgrades where supported. also scheduling a maintenance window tomorrow 03:00-06:00 UTC for the canary kernel revert and driver forward tests.
alex: add automatic rollback triggers: if any host sees >3 Xids in 2h post-change, revert to previous known-good config.
ben: agreed. SLO for rollout: keep overall Xid rate under 0.5/host/day in canary tier.
loren: I'll prepare a small playbook with exact rpm/kernel packages and the `nvidia-smi --query` commands we used. snippet: ```
sudo apt-get install --allow-downgrades linux-image-5.19.8
sudo dpkg -i nvidia-driver-540.14.deb
reboot && sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -f | grep -i xid
```
marta: thanks — I'll post postmortem if the maintenance uncovers anything unexpected. also calling out cost/ops: if we need to drain 12 hosts and replace, estimated replacement budget ~ $38k (capex) + 2w provisioning lead time.
alex: underwritable in next infra spend cycle if we push. for now prioritize avoiding mass customer impact.
ben: final ask: oncall, please watch the canary channel during the window and escalate if rollback condition hits. I'll create a grafana alert with the threshold. :thumbsup:
marta: copy. pinging @alex @loren once maintenance starts. :rotating_light:
